label: rem:general-link-condition
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:general-link-condition}
The specific form of softplus is not essential for
Theorems~\ref{thm:affine-boundary}--\ref{thm:affine-supercritical}.
A convenient sufficient condition under which all their conclusions remain
valid is to replace \(s_c\) by a \(C^1\) strictly increasing bijection
\(\ell:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)\) satisfying
\[
 0<\ell'(x)\leq1,
 \qquad
 \ell(x)-x=O(x^{-A})\quad(x\to\infty)
 \quad\text{for every }A>0.
\]
Nonexpansiveness and the second condition imply \(\ell(x)\geq x\).  The
link correction is therefore negligible in the high-state increment
expansions, so the boundary moment index \(\kappa\) is unchanged.
Monotonicity supplies the association argument in the long-memory regime,
whereas nonexpansiveness supplies filter contraction, coupling, and the
high-state persistence bounds.  Strict positivity prevents the state from
being absorbed at zero.  The smooth bijection condition is used for the
change of variables and ensures differentiability of the likelihood function.
The ReLU limit \(\max(x,0)\), however, lies outside this class because it is
neither strictly positive nor a \(C^1\) bijection.

label: lem:softplus-supercritical-fixed-points
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:softplus-supercritical-fixed-points}
Let \(\phi>1\) and consider the deterministic map
\[
 \Psi_\phi(m)=s_c(\omega+\phi m),\qquad m>0.
\]
Define
\[
 \omega_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)
 =c[(\phi-1)\log(\phi-1)-\phi\log\phi],
 \qquad
 m_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)
 =c\log\left(\frac{\phi}{\phi-1}\right),
\]
where ``SN'' means saddle-node. We have  $\omega_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)<0$, and furthermore, if \(\omega<\omega_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)\), then \(\Psi_\phi\) has exactly two
positive fixed points \(m_-<m_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)<m_+\), with the lower (resp. upper) fixed
point being locally attracting (resp. repelling); if \(\omega=\omega_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)\), there is a unique, double fixed point \(m_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)\); if
\(\omega>\omega_{\mathrm{SN}}(\phi)\), there is no positive fixed point.

label: thm:affine-qmle

body_md:
\label{thm:affine-qmle}
{
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:affine-seed} and \ref{ass:invertibility}
hold, the observations come from a stationary and ergodic solution of
\eqref{eq:affine-softplus-model} at \(\theta_0\), and \(\theta_0\) is an
interior point of the compact set \(\Theta_Q\) defined above.  Put
\(\phi_0=\alpha_0+\beta_0\), and suppose either
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \(\phi_0<1\) and \(\alpha_0\neq0\); or
\item[(ii)] \(\phi_0=1\), \(\omega_0<0\), and
\(\kappa_0:=-2\omega_0/(\alpha_0^2\sigma_0^2)>1\).
\end{enumerate}
Then the conditional-mean filter is identified at \(\theta_0\) over
\(\Theta_Q\), \(I_0\) is positive definite,
\(\widehat\theta_n\to\theta_0\) almost surely,
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)
 \Rightarrow N(0,\sigma_0^2I_0^{-1}),
\]
and \(\widehat\sigma_n^2\to\sigma_0^2\) and
\(\widehat I_{Q,n}\to I_0\) in probability.
}

title: Example
body_md:
Here \(\sigma_0^2=1\), and \(Q_n-\sum_{t=1}^n\log(X_t!)\) is the exact
conditional log-likelihood.  Thus the QMLE is the conditional MLE, with
first-order covariance \(I_0^{-1}/n\), where \(I_0\) is the conditional

delta method gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\kappa(\widehat\omega_n,\widehat\alpha_n)-\kappa_0)
 \Rightarrow
 N(0,g_0^\top I_0^{-1}g_0).
\]

label: lem:softplus-calculus
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:softplus-calculus}
Fix \(c>0\), and set
\(p_c=s_c'\), \(r_c=(\log s_c)'\), \(r_c'=(\log s_c)''\), and
\(j_c=p_c^2/s_c\).  For a constant \(C=C(c)\) and all \(x\),
\begin{align}
&0<p_c\leq1,\quad 0\leq s_c''\leq(4c)^{-1},\quad
 p_c/s_c\leq c^{-1},\quad s_c''/s_c\leq c^{-2},
 \label{eq:softplus-self-regularization}\\
&p_c\leq C\frac{s_c}{1+s_c},\quad
 r_c\leq\frac C{1+s_c},\quad
 s_c''+|r_c'|\leq C\frac{s_c}{(1+s_c)^3},
 \label{eq:qmle-sharp-softplus-derivatives}\\
&0\leq j_c\leq c^{-1},\qquad |j_c'|\leq3c^{-2}.
 \label{eq:softplus-information-calculus}
\end{align}
Also \(|\log s_c(x)|\leq C(1+|x|)\).  The bounds on \(p_c=s_c'\) and
\(r_c=(\log s_c)'\) imply that \(s_c\) and \(\log s_c\) are
\(1\)- and \(1/c\)-Lipschitz, respectively.  The functions \(p_c,r_c,j_c\)
and their derivatives are bounded.
head: environment
name: Softplus calculus

title: Proof
body_md:
Set \(u=e^{x/c}\) and \(v=\log(1+u)\).  Direct differentiation gives
\[
 s_c=cv,\qquad p_c=\frac{u}{1+u},\qquad
 s_c''=\frac{u}{c(1+u)^2},\qquad
 r_c'=\frac{u(v-u)}{c^2(1+u)^2v^2}.
\]
Use \(u/(1+u)\leq v\).  For \(u\leq1\), use
\(u/2\leq v\leq u\) and \(0\leq u-v\leq u^2/2\); for \(u\geq1\), use
\(v\geq\log2\) and \(\sup_{u\geq1}v^2/u<\infty\).  These prove the derivative
bounds.  The comparisons \(ce^{x/c}/2\leq s_c(x)\leq ce^{x/c}\) for
\(x\leq0\) and \(c\log2\leq s_c(x)\leq x+c\log2\) for \(x\geq0\)
give the log bound.  Finally,
\(j_c'=2p_c s_c''/s_c-p_c^3/s_c^2\), which gives
\eqref{eq:softplus-information-calculus}.

label: lem:unrestricted-candidate-filter
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:unrestricted-candidate-filter}
Let \((X_t)\) be any stationary nonnegative process with
\(\mathbb{E} X_0<\infty\).  Suppose that \(\Theta_Q\) is compact and
\(\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_Q}|\beta|\leq\rho_\beta<1\).  Then, for every
\(\theta\in\Theta_Q\), the candidate version of
recursion~\eqref{mrecursion} has a unique stationary causal solution
\(M_t(\theta)\).  It is continuous in \(\theta\)
almost surely and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_Q}M_t(\theta)
 \leq C\sum_{j=0}^\infty\rho_\beta^j(1+X_{t-1-j})<\infty
 \quad\text{a.s.}
\]
For any two starting values driven by the same observations,
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_Q}
 |M_t^{(1)}(\theta)-M_t^{(2)}(\theta)|
 \leq\rho_\beta^t\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_Q}
 |M_0^{(1)}(\theta)-M_0^{(2)}(\theta)|.
\]
Moreover, if, for some \(\theta\in\Theta_Q\), a jointly stationary pair
\((X_t,M_t^*)\) with \(\mathbb{E} M_0^*<\infty\) satisfies the same recursion, then
\(M_t^*=M_t(\theta)\) almost surely.  In particular, the stationary state
is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}^{X}\)-measurable.
These conclusions do not require \(\alpha+\beta<1\) for the candidate
parameter.
head: environment
name: Uniform invertibility of the candidate mean recursion

title: Proof
body_md:
This is the uniformly contractive case of the stochastic-recurrence
construction in \citet{bougerol1993} and
\citet[Theorem~2.8]{straumannMikosch2006}.  Because those results assume
ergodic driving maps, we give a direct proof for merely stationary \(X_t\)
that also records the explicit uniform bounds.
For \(F_{t,\theta}(m)=s_c(\omega+\alpha X_{t-1}+\beta m)\), the
one-Lipschitz property of \(s_c\) gives, uniformly in \(\theta\),
\[
 |F_{t,\theta}(m)-F_{t,\theta}(m')|
 \leq\rho_\beta|m-m'|,
 \qquad
 F_{t,\theta}(0)\leq C(1+X_{t-1}).
\]
Successive backward iterates from zero differ by at most
\(C\rho_\beta^j(1+X_{t-1-j})\), whose sum has finite expectation.  Hence
they converge uniformly in \(\theta\), almost surely, to a shift-equivariant
causal solution \(M_t\).  The tail error is bounded by
\(C\sum_{j\geq k}\rho_\beta^j(1+X_{t-1-j})\to0\) almost surely.  Each finite
iterate is continuous in \(\theta\), so \(M_t(\cdot)\) is continuous.
Iteration of \(F_{t,\theta}(m)\leq F_{t,\theta}(0)+\rho_\beta m\) gives the
stated envelope, and forward contraction gives the initialization bound.

Let \(\bar M\) be either \(M^*\) or another stationary causal solution at the
same parameter.  The comparison pair is jointly stationary, and for every
\(j\geq1\),
\[
 |\bar M_t-M_t(\theta)|
 \leq\rho_\beta^j
 |\bar M_{t-j}-M_{t-j}(\theta)|.
\]
For \(\bar M=M^*\), take expectations and let \(j\to\infty\).  For an
arbitrary stationary causal \(\bar M\), the right side converges to zero in
probability because the factor following \(\rho_\beta^j\) has a fixed finite
distribution.  Thus \(\bar M_t=M_t(\theta)\) almost surely in both cases.

label: lem:affine-concentration
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:affine-concentration}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:affine-seed}, for every \(\epsilon>0\) and
\(A>0\), there is \(C_{\epsilon,A}<\infty\) such that, for \(m\geq1\),
\[
 \Pr(|U_m|>\epsilon m)\leq C_{\epsilon,A}m^{-A}.
\]
For every fixed \(\chi>0\),
\[
 \mathbb{E}(W_m+1)^\chi\leq C_\chi(1+m^\chi).
\]
For every fixed \(\chi\geq2\),
\[
 \mathbb{E}|U_m|^\chi\leq C_\chi(1+m^{\chi/2}).
\]
For every \(m>0\), \(G_m\) has unbounded support.
head: environment
name: Moments and polynomial concentration

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix an even integer \(k\geq2\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:affine-seed}(i)
gives \(\mathbb{E} W_1^k<\infty\).  For \(0\leq s\leq1\), the convolution
identity \(G_s*G_{1-s}=G_1\) permits a realization
\(W_1=W_s+W_{1-s}'\) with nonnegative independent summands.  Hence
\(W_s\leq W_1\) under this realization, and
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq1}\mathbb{E}|W_s-s|^k
 \leq 2^{k-1}(\mathbb{E} W_1^k+1)<\infty.
\]

Using the decomposition \(m=j_m+r_m\) introduced in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-conditional-clt}, the convolution identity
for the affine family permits a realization of \(W_m-m\) as the
sum of \(j_m\) independent copies of \(U_1\), together with an
independent random variable distributed as \(U_{r_m}\).
Rosenthal's inequality gives, for every even integer \(k\geq2\),
\[
 \mathbb{E}|U_m|^k\leq C_k(1+m^{k/2}).
\]
For any real \(\chi\geq2\), choose an even integer \(k\geq\chi\);
Lyapunov's inequality then gives the stated moment bound of order \(\chi\).
The same decomposition, together with
\(W_m\leq m+|U_m|\), proves the stated raw-moment bound for every
\(\chi\geq2\); Lyapunov's inequality applied to the second raw moment covers
\(0<\chi<2\).

For any prescribed \(A>0\), choose \(\chi\geq2\) with \(\chi/2>A\).
Markov's inequality then gives
\[
 \Pr(|U_m|>\epsilon m)
 \leq \frac{C_\chi(1+m^{\chi/2})}{\epsilon^\chi m^\chi}
 \leq C_{\epsilon,A}m^{-A}.
\]
Under the density alternative, unbounded support follows from strict
positivity on \((0,\infty)\).  Under finite activity, \(G_m\) is compound
Poisson; positive variance gives a nonzero jump, and arbitrarily many such
jumps have positive probability.

label: lem:affine-state-observation-moments
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: State--observation moment equivalence

title: Proof
body_md:
If \(\mathbb{E} M^s<\infty\), the raw-moment bound in
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration} gives \(\mathbb{E} X^s<\infty\).
Conversely, when \(m\geq8\sigma^2\), conditional Chebyshev gives
\(\Pr(X\geq m/2\mid M=m)\geq1/2\), and therefore
\[
 \mathbb{E} X^s\geq2^{-s-1}
 \mathbb{E}[M^s\mathbf1_{\{M\geq8\sigma^2\}}],
\]
so \(\mathbb{E} X^s<\infty\) implies \(\mathbb{E} M^s<\infty\).

label: lem:affine-cancellation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Affine softplus cancellation

title: Proof
body_md:
The elementary softplus bound
\[
 0\leq s_c(x)-\max(x,0)\leq c\log2,
 \qquad x\in\mathbb R,
\]
and the one-Lipschitz property of \(x\mapsto\max(x,0)\) give
\[
 \left|
 \frac{s_c(\omega+\alpha W_m+\beta m)}{m}-\max(\phi,0)
 \right|
 \leq\frac{|\omega|+|\alpha||U_m|+c\log2}{m}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration}, together with the exact second moment
when \(0<\chi<2\), makes the right-hand side converge to zero in
\(L^\chi\).  Thus the normalized update converges to \(\max(\phi,0)\) in
\(L^\chi\); convergence of its moments of order \(\chi\) proves the claim.

label: lem:affine-boundary-expansions
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:affine-boundary-expansions}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:affine-seed}, suppose \(\phi=1\), and set
\[
 Y_m=\omega+m+\alpha U_m,
 \qquad \Delta_m=s_c(Y_m)-m.
\]
Then, for every \(A>0\),
\begin{align}
 \mathbb{E}\Delta_m&=\omega+O(m^{-A}),\label{eq:affine-delta-mean}\\
 \mathbb{E}\Delta_m^2&=\alpha^2\sigma^2m+O(1).\label{eq:affine-delta-var}
\end{align}
For every fixed \(\chi>1\),
\begin{align}
 \mathbb{E}[s_c(Y_m)^\chi-m^\chi]
 &=\chi m^{\chi-1}\left[\omega+
       \frac{\chi-1}{2}\alpha^2\sigma^2+o(1)\right].
 \label{eq:affine-power-drift}\\
 \mathbb{E}\!\left[\sqrt{s_c(Y_m)}-\sqrt m\right]
 &=\frac{4\omega-\alpha^2\sigma^2}{8\sqrt m}+O(m^{-1}),
 \label{eq:affine-sqrt-drift}\\
 \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\sqrt{s_c(Y_m)}-\sqrt m\right)^2\right]
 &=\frac{\alpha^2\sigma^2}{4}+O(m^{-1/2}).
 \label{eq:affine-sqrt-variance}
\end{align}
head: environment
name: Affine boundary expansions

label: eq:softplus-remainder-superpolynomial
title: Proof
body_md:
Choose \(\epsilon>0\) so small that \(1-|\alpha|\epsilon>0\).  On
\(\{|U_m|\leq\epsilon m\}\),
\[
 Y_m=\omega+m+\alpha U_m
 \geq \omega+(1-|\alpha|\epsilon)m.
\]
Hence, for all sufficiently large \(m\), \(Y_m\) is positive and bounded
above and below by positive multiples of \(m\), so the softplus remainder
\({\mathcal E_m}=s_c(Y_m)-Y_m\) is exponentially small.  Globally,
\[
 0\leq {\mathcal E_m}\leq c\log2+\max(-Y_m,0)
       \leq C(1+m+|U_m|).
\]
Consequently, Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration} and H\"older's
inequality imply that, for every fixed \(j\geq0\), \(\ell\geq1\), and
\(A>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}[(1+|U_m|)^j{\mathcal E_m}^\ell]=O(m^{-A}).
 \label{eq:softplus-remainder-superpolynomial}
\end{equation}
Indeed, the contribution of \(\{|U_m|\leq\epsilon m\}\) is an
exponential times a polynomial.  On its complement, choose both the
moment and the polynomial concentration order in
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration} large enough for the desired
H\"older bound.

Since
\(\Delta_m=\omega+\alpha U_m+{\mathcal E_m}\),
\eqref{eq:softplus-remainder-superpolynomial} and the centered moment
bounds prove \eqref{eq:affine-delta-mean}--\eqref{eq:affine-delta-var}.
They also give, for every fixed \(p\geq2\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}|\Delta_m|^p\leq C_p(1+m^{p/2}).
 \label{eq:affine-delta-absolute-moments}
\end{equation}

For a sufficiently small fixed \(\eta>0\), the event
\(\{|\Delta_m|>\eta m\}\) also has probability smaller than every
prescribed inverse power of \(m\).  On its complement, Taylor's formula
gives
\[
 (m+\Delta_m)^\chi-m^\chi
 =\chi m^{\chi-1}\Delta_m
  +\frac{\chi(\chi-1)}2m^{\chi-2}\Delta_m^2
  +O(m^{\chi-3}|\Delta_m|^3).
\]
The absolute third-moment bound makes the remainder
\(O(m^{\chi-3/2})\), which is \(o(m^{\chi-1})\).  On the complementary event, H\"older's
inequality, arbitrary-order polynomial concentration, and sufficiently
high moments give the same \(o(m^{\chi-1})\) conclusion.  Substitution of
the first two increment moments gives
\eqref{eq:affine-power-drift}.  On \(\{|\Delta_m|\leq\eta m\}\),
Taylor's formula also gives
\[
 \sqrt{m+\Delta_m}-\sqrt m
 =\frac{\Delta_m}{2m^{1/2}}
 -\frac{\Delta_m^2}{8m^{3/2}}
 +O\!\left(\frac{|\Delta_m|^3}{m^{5/2}}\right),
\]
and
\[
 (\sqrt{m+\Delta_m}-\sqrt m)^2
 =\frac{\Delta_m^2}{4m}
  +O\!\left(\frac{|\Delta_m|^3}{m^2}\right).
\]
Using \eqref{eq:affine-delta-absolute-moments} with \(p=3\) and treating
the complementary event as above therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}(\sqrt{m+\Delta_m}-\sqrt m)
 =\frac{\mathbb{E}\Delta_m}{2\sqrt m}
  -\frac{\mathbb{E}\Delta_m^2}{8m^{3/2}}+O(m^{-1})
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb{E}(\sqrt{m+\Delta_m}-\sqrt m)^2
 =\frac{\mathbb{E}\Delta_m^2}{4m}+O(m^{-1/2}),
\]
which prove \eqref{eq:affine-sqrt-drift}--
\eqref{eq:affine-sqrt-variance}.

label: lem:affine-uniform-root-increments
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:affine-uniform-root-increments}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:affine-seed}, suppose \(\phi=1\), and define
\[
 \Delta_m^{(1/2)}=\sqrt{s_c(\omega+m+\alpha U_m)}-\sqrt m.
\]
For every fixed \(p>0\),
\[
 \sup_{m\geq0}\mathbb{E}|\Delta_m^{(1/2)}|^p<\infty.
\]
head: environment
name: Uniform square-root increments

title: Proof
body_md:
{
For \(m\geq0\), the one-Lipschitz property of \(s_c\) and
\(0\leq s_c(m)-m\leq c\log2\) give
\[
 |s_c(\omega+m+\alpha U_m)-m|
 \leq |\omega|+|\alpha||U_m|+c\log2.
\]
Thus, for \(m\geq1\),
\[
 |\Delta_m^{(1/2)}|
 =\frac{|s_c(\omega+m+\alpha U_m)-m|}
 {\sqrt{s_c(\omega+m+\alpha U_m)}+\sqrt m}
 \leq\frac{|\omega|+|\alpha||U_m|+c\log2}{\sqrt m}.
\]
For \(p\geq2\), the centered-moment bound in
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration} now gives
\(\sup_{m\geq1}\mathbb{E}|\Delta_m^{(1/2)}|^p<\infty\).
For \(0<p<2\), the same conclusion follows from
\(\mathbb{E}|\Delta_m^{(1/2)}|^p
\leq(\mathbb{E}|\Delta_m^{(1/2)}|^2)^{p/2}\).
For \(0\leq m\leq1\), the elementary softplus bound gives
\(|\Delta_m^{(1/2)}|^p\leq C_p(1+W_m^{p/2})\),
whose expectation is uniformly bounded by the raw-moment bound in
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration}, for every \(p>0\).
}

label: lem:affine-boundary-nonconfinement
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:affine-boundary-nonconfinement}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:affine-seed} and \ref{ass:invertibility}, suppose
\(\phi=1\).  For every initial state \(m\geq0\) and every intercept \(\omega\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\limsup_{t\to\infty}M_t=\infty\,\middle|\,M_0=m\right)=1.

head: environment
name: Boundary nonconfinement

title: Proof
body_md:
Here \(\alpha=1-\beta>0\).  Fix \(K>0\) and put
\(\ell_K=s_c(\omega+\min(\beta,0)K)>0\).
If \(M_t\leq K\), then \(M_{t+1}\geq\ell_K\).  For \(m\geq\ell_K\),
the convolution identity makes \(G_m\) stochastically dominate
\(G_{\ell_K}\).  Choose \(z_K\) with
\(s_c(\omega+\alpha z_K+\min(\beta,0)K)>K\).
The unbounded support of \(G_{\ell_K}\) then gives, uniformly over
\(0\leq m\leq K\),
\[
 \Pr(\max(M_1,M_2)>K\mid M_0=m)
 \geq G_{\ell_K}([z_K,\infty))=:\delta_K>0.
\]
The Markov property bounds the probability of remaining in \([0,K]\)
for the next \(2n\) steps by \((1-\delta_K)^n\).  Apply this bound after
each deterministic time and intersect over positive integer \(K\).

title: Proof
body_md:

Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-uniform-root-increments}, with \(s(x)=\sqrt x\)
for large \(x\).  That lemma
gives uniform moments of every order, so truncation changes these first
two moments by an arbitrarily high inverse power of \(x\).
Equations~\eqref{eq:affine-sqrt-drift}--\eqref{eq:affine-sqrt-variance}
therefore give, for any fixed \(\delta\in(0,1)\) and all large \(x\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{2\mu_1^{[s]}(x)}{\mu_2^{[s]}(x)}
 =\frac{4\omega/(\alpha^2\sigma^2)-1}{x}+O(x^{-2})
 \geq-\frac1x-\frac{1-\delta}{x\log x}.
 \label{eq:affine-lamperti-ratio-rigorous}
\end{equation}
The same estimates imply
\(\mu_1(x)\geq-C/x\) for large \(x\),
\(\sup_{x\geq0}\mu_2(x)<\infty\), and
\(\liminf_{x\to\infty}\mu_2^{[s]}(x)>0\).
Moreover, uniform increment moments give
\[
 \mathbb{E}[|\xi(x)|^3\mathbf1_{\{-s(x)\leq\xi(x)\leq0\}}]=O(1)=o(x/\log x),
 \qquad
 \Pr\{\xi(x)\leq-s(x)\}=o((x^2\log x)^{-1}).
\]
These are conditions~(2.60)--(2.62), (2.65), and (2.66) of
\citet[Corollary~2.12]{denisov2025markov}, with iterated-logarithm index
\(m=1\).  That corollary yields an \(r_0<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}[T_r\mid R_0=x]=\infty\quad(x>r\geq r_0),
 \qquad T_r=\inf\{t\geq0:R_t\leq r\}.
 \label{eq:affine-infinite-mean-passage}
\end{equation}

If \(\pi_R\) were invariant, strict positivity of softplus would give
\(\pi_R(\{0\})=0\).  Choose \(r\geq r_0\) with
\(\pi_R(A)>0\), where \(A=(0,r]\), and let
\(T_A^+=\inf\{t\geq1:R_t\in A\}\).
For every \(x\in A\), the unbounded support of \(G_{x^2}\) and
\(\alpha>0\) give \(\Pr(R_1>r\mid R_0=x)>0\).  The Markov property and
\eqref{eq:affine-infinite-mean-passage} imply
\(\mathbb{E}[T_A^+\mid R_0=x]=\infty\).
Let \(\Pr_{\pi_R}\) denote probability under the two-sided stationary law
with marginal distribution \(\pi_R\).  Then
\[
\begin{split}
 \int_A\mathbb{E}[T_A^+\mid R_0=x]\,\pi_R(dx)
 &=\sum_{j\geq0}\Pr\nolimits_{\pi_R}\{R_0\in A,R_1,\ldots,R_j\notin A\}\\
 &=\sum_{j\geq0}\Pr\nolimits_{\pi_R}\{R_{-j}\in A,R_{-j+1},\ldots,R_0\notin A\}
 \leq1.
\end{split}
\]
For \(j=0\) the event is \(\{R_0\in A\}\); the events in the last sum
are disjoint, specifying the most recent visit to \(A\) at or before
time zero.  This contradicts \(\pi_R(A)>0\) and proves the claim.

label: lem:finite-activity-wasserstein-coupling
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Finite-activity coupling and observation mixing

label: eq:affine-tv-similarity
title: Proof
body_md:
Use the activity rate \(L_{\rm act}\) defined in
Section~\ref{sec:affine-extension}, and put \(\rho_\beta=|\beta|<1\).
For current states \(m\leq m'\), draw
\(W_m\sim G_m\) and \(V_{m'-m}\sim G_{m'-m}\) independently, and set
\(W_{m'}=W_m+V_{m'-m}\).  The convolution identity gives
\(W_{m'}\sim G_{m'}\).  Define the next states by
\[
 M^+=s_c(\omega+\alpha W_m+\beta m),
 \qquad
 M'^+=s_c(\omega+\alpha W_{m'}+\beta m').
\]
The kernel \(Q((m,m'),\cdot)\) is the joint distribution of
\((M^+,M'^+)\); explicitly, for every Borel set \(B\subseteq E\times E\),
\[
 Q((m,m'),B)=\Pr((M^+,M'^+)\in B).
\]
For \(m>m'\), reverse the roles of the two coordinates in this
construction.  Each next-state coordinate has the transition law
specified by \(P\), so \(Q\) is a coupling kernel for \(P\).
The observation coupling gives
\begin{equation}
 \lVert G_m-G_{m'}\rVert_{\rm TV}
 \leq\Pr(W_m\ne W_{m'})
 =1-e^{-L_{\rm act}|m-m'|}.
 \label{eq:affine-tv-similarity}
\end{equation}
For the finite-activity examples in Table~\ref{tab:affine-seeds},
\(L_{\rm Pois}=1\), \(L_{\rm NB}=(p/(1-p))\log(1/p)\),
\(L_{\rm ARG0}=1/\tau\), and \(L_{\rm Tw}=1/(\nu\tau)\).
At each step, apply this construction to the current pair of states.
All probabilities for the paired process below refer to this coupling.
When observations
agree, the next state distance is at most \(\rho_\beta\) times the
current distance.  Thus, from initial distance \(D=|m-m'|\),
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(X_j=X'_j\text{ for all }j\geq0\mid M_0=m,M'_0=m')
 \geq\exp(-L_{\rm act}D/(1-\rho_\beta))>0.
 \label{eq:finite-activity-permanent-agreement}
\end{equation}
On this event the state distance tends to zero.  Starting from any two
ergodic invariant laws and integrating this strictly positive bound gives
a positive-probability asymptotic coupling.  By
\mbox{\citet[Theorem~1.1]{hairerMattinglyScheutzow2011}} the laws coincide;
ergodic decomposition proves uniqueness without any moment assumption.

Fix \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) with
\(a_0=\rho_\beta^q+L_{\rm act}\varepsilon<1\), and set
\(d(m,m')=1\wedge(D/\varepsilon)^q\).
For \(D<\varepsilon\), the coupling gives
\[
 (Qd)(m,m')\leq\rho_\beta^q d(m,m')+L_{\rm act}D
 \leq a_0d(m,m'),
\]
whereas for \(D\geq\varepsilon\), \(Qd\leq1=d\).
On \([0,R]^2\), choose \(N_R\) with
\((\rho_\beta^{N_R}R/\varepsilon)^q\leq1/2\).
The agreement event has probability at least
\(p_R=e^{-L_{\rm act}R/(1-\rho_\beta)}\), so
\(Q^{N_R}d\leq1-p_R/2\) there.
Combining this with \(Q^{N_R}d\leq Qd\leq a_0d\) when \(d<1\)
proves \eqref{eq:finite-activity-coupling-set}, with
\(\delta_R=\min(1-a_0,p_R/2)\).

Let \(K(m,\cdot)\) be the law of the entire observation future
\((X_0,X_1,\ldots)\) from state \(m\).
If the initial state has distribution \(\mu\), the corresponding
observation-future distribution is
\[
 (\mu K)(B)=\int K(m,B)\,\mu(dm),
\]
for every measurable set \(B\) of observation paths.
Equation~\eqref{eq:finite-activity-permanent-agreement} implies
\[
 \|K(m,\cdot)-K(m',\cdot)\|_{\rm TV}
 \leq1-e^{-L_{\rm act}D/(1-\rho_\beta)}\leq C d(m,m').
\]
Integrating over a coupling gives
\(\|\mu K-\nu K\|_{\rm TV}\leq C\mathcal W_d(\mu,\nu)\).
Given the observation past through time zero, the future starting at
\(n\) has conditional law
\(\mathbb{E}[P^{n-1}(M_1,\cdot)K\mid\mathcal F_0^X]\).
Convexity of total variation and stationarity of \(M_1\) now give
\eqref{eq:finite-activity-wasserstein-beta}.

label: lem:infinite-activity-density-overlap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:infinite-activity-density-overlap}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:affine-seed} and
\ref{ass:invertibility} hold through the infinite-activity
positive-density alternative, and \(\alpha>0\).  If \(\beta<0\),
every interval of positive length in
\((0,\infty)\) is reachable with positive probability from every initial
state.  If \(0\leq\beta<1\), let
\(m_\beta=s_c(\omega+\beta m_\beta)\).  Every initial state then enters
\((m_\beta,\infty)\) almost surely and remains there.
On the relevant region---\((0,\infty)\) when \(\beta<0\), and
\((m_\beta,\infty)\) when \(0\leq\beta<1\)---the state chain is
irreducible and strongly aperiodic, and every bounded set is petite.
Every invariant law on the original state space is supported on this
region.
Moreover, for every \(0<R<\infty\), there are \(\epsilon_R>0\) and a
probability measure \(\nu_R\), common to all initial states
\(m\in(0,R]\), such that, for every Borel set \(A\subseteq(0,\infty)\),
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(M_2\in A\mid M_0=m)\geq\epsilon_R\nu_R(A),
 \qquad 0<m\leq R.
 \label{eq:density-two-step-overlap}
\end{equation}
In addition, within the relevant irreducible state region there are a compact
interval \(D\), a constant \(\epsilon_D>0\), and a probability measure
\(\nu_D\) supported on \(D\) such that, for every Borel set
\(A\subseteq(0,\infty)\),
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(M_1\in A\mid M_0=m)\geq\epsilon_D\nu_D(A),
 \qquad m\in D.
 \label{eq:density-one-step-self-overlap}
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Overlap for infinite-activity density families

label: eq:density-state-kernel
title: Proof
body_md:
Using the conditional density \(g(m,x)\) from Assumption~\ref{ass:affine-seed}, write
\[
 h_c(y)=s_c^{-1}(y)=c\log(e^{y/c}-1),
 \qquad
 f_0(m)=s_c(\omega+\beta m).
\]
The transition kernel of the state chain has density
\begin{equation}
 p(m,y)=\frac{h_c'(y)}{\alpha}
 g\!\left(m,\frac{h_c(y)-\omega-\beta m}{\alpha}\right)
 \mathbf 1_{\{y>f_0(m)\}}.
 \label{eq:density-state-kernel}
\end{equation}
It is jointly continuous and strictly positive on compact subsets of
\(\{(m,y):m>0,\ y>f_0(m)\}\).

We first establish the two-step minorization
\eqref{eq:density-two-step-overlap}.  Fix \(R>0\).
For \(0<m\leq R\), Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \Pr(X_0\leq2R\mid M_0=m)\geq\frac12.
\]
On this event, \(M_1\) lies in the fixed compact interval
\[
 K_R=[u_R,v_R],\qquad
 u_R=s_c(\omega+\min(\beta,0)R)>0,\quad
 v_R=s_c(\omega+(2\alpha+\max(\beta,0))R)<\infty.
\]
Choose a compact interval \(J_R=[a_R,b_R]\) with
\(a_R>\sup_{z\in K_R}f_0(z)\).  By
\eqref{eq:density-state-kernel},
\[
 d_R=\inf_{z\in K_R,\,y\in J_R}p(z,y)>0.
\]
If \(\nu_R\) is normalized Lebesgue measure on \(J_R\), the Markov
property therefore yields, for every Borel set \(A\subseteq(0,\infty)\),
\[
 \Pr(M_2\in A\mid M_0=m)\geq\frac{d_R|J_R|}{2}\nu_R(A),
 \qquad 0<m\leq R.
\]
Thus every bounded set has a common two-step probability component,
uniformly down to a state approaching zero.

It remains to identify the state region connected by the density.  If
\(\beta<0\), then
\(f_0(z)\downarrow0\) as \(z\to\infty\).  Positivity of
\eqref{eq:density-state-kernel} shows that any state can first reach a
neighborhood of a sufficiently large \(z\) and can then reach every
positive-Lebesgue-measure subset of \((0,\infty)\).

If \(0\leq\beta<1\), \(f_0\) is a contraction and has the unique fixed
point \(m_\beta\).  Write \(f_0^{\circ n}\) for its \(n\)-fold
composition.  For \(m>m_\beta\),
 \(m_\beta\leq f_0(m)<m\), and induction in
\eqref{eq:density-state-kernel} shows that \(P^n(m,\cdot)\) has a density
positive on \((f_0^{\circ n}(m),\infty)\).  Since
\(f_0^{\circ n}(m)\to m_\beta\), every positive-Lebesgue-measure subset of
\((m_\beta,\infty)\) can eventually be reached.  Let
\(E_\beta=(m_\beta,\infty)\).  This set is absorbing because the transition
support satisfies \(y>f_0(m)\geq m_\beta\) for \(m\in E_\beta\).  In the preceding two-step
minorization, take \(R=m_\beta\) and choose \(J_R\subset E_\beta\).  Then, for
some \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \inf_{0<m\leq m_\beta}P^2(m,E_\beta)\geq\epsilon.
\]
Consequently, if \(T_{E_\beta}=\inf\{t\geq0:M_t\in E_\beta\}\), the Markov property
gives
\[
 \Pr(T_{E_\beta}>2n\mid M_0=m)\leq(1-\epsilon)^n,
 \qquad 0<m\leq m_\beta.
\]
From the extended state zero, the chain first moves deterministically to
\(s_c(\omega)>0\).  Thus every initial state enters \(E_\beta\) almost surely
and remains there, and
\(P^n(m,E_\beta)\to1\) for every initial state.  Hence, for any invariant law
\(\mu\), invariance and dominated convergence yield
\[
 \mu(E_\beta)=\int P^n(m,E_\beta)\,\mu(dm)\longrightarrow1.
\]
Thus every invariant law is supported on the relevant region.  For
\(\beta<0\), that region is the whole state space.

Finally, in either class choose a compact interval \([a,b]\) such that
\(a>\sup_{m\in[a,b]}f_0(m)\).  The density in
\eqref{eq:density-state-kernel} is bounded below on \([a,b]^2\), so this
interval has a one-step common probability component supported on itself.
The reachability results give irreducibility on the relevant region,
\eqref{eq:density-two-step-overlap} makes every bounded set petite, and the
one-step component supported on \([a,b]\) gives strong aperiodicity.

label: lem:feller-invariant-limits
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:feller-invariant-limits}
Let \(E\) be a Polish state space and \(P\) a Feller kernel on \(E\).
(i) If \(\mu_N=N^{-1}\sum_{j<N}P^j(x,\cdot)\) is tight, each weak limit
is \(P\)-invariant.  (ii) If \(P_n\) has invariant law \(\pi_n\),
\((\pi_n)\) is tight, and \(P_nf\to Pf\) locally uniformly for every
bounded Lipschitz \(f\), each weak limit of \((\pi_n)\) is \(P\)-invariant.
In either case, \(P(x,B)=0\) for all \(x\) forces every such limit to give
\(B\) zero mass.
head: environment
name: Feller compactness and invariant limits

title: Proof
body_md:
For (i), \(\mu_N(Pf-f)=(P^Nf(x)-f(x))/N\to0\) for bounded continuous
\(f\), and the Feller property permits passage to a weak limit.  For (ii),
tightness and local uniform convergence give
\(\pi_n(P_nf-Pf)\to0\), while \(\pi_nPf\to\pi Pf\); pass to the limit in
\(\pi_nf=\pi_nP_nf\).  Bounded Lipschitz functions determine probability
laws.  Finally,
\(\pi(B)=\int P(x,B)\,\pi(dx)=0\).

name: Association

title: Proof
body_md:
The convolution identity \(G_{m'}=G_m*G_{m'-m}\), \(m'\geq m\), shows
that \(G_m\) is stochastically increasing in \(m\).  Hence its
generalized quantile \(F_m^{\leftarrow}(u)\), \(0<u<1\), may be chosen jointly
measurable and nondecreasing in both arguments.  Indeed, weak continuity
of \(m\mapsto G_m\) makes \((m,x)\mapsto G_m([0,x])\) a Borel
distribution function, and one may take
\[
 F_m^{\leftarrow}(u)=\inf\{x\geq0:G_m([0,x])\geq u\}.
\]
The definition makes \(F_m^{\leftarrow}\) nondecreasing in \(u\), while stochastic
ordering makes it nondecreasing in \(m\).  Let
\(\mathcal U_0,\mathcal U_1,\ldots\) be
independent uniform random
variables, independent of an invariant initial state \(M_0\), and put
\(X_t=F_{M_t}^{\leftarrow}(\mathcal U_t)\) and
\(M_{t+1}=s_c(\omega+\alpha X_t+\beta M_t)\).
Because \(\alpha>0\), \(\beta\geq0\), and \(s_c\) is increasing, every
finite observation vector is a coordinatewise nondecreasing function of
the independent variables \(M_0,\mathcal U_0,\mathcal U_1,\ldots\).  Independent variables
are associated, and association is preserved by coordinatewise
nondecreasing transformations; see \citet{esary1967association}.

label: lem:affine-boundary-invariant-tail
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Boundary invariant tail

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the square-root chain \(R_t\), with increment \(\xi(x)\) as defined
after Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-uniform-root-increments}.  Write
\[
 b=\frac{\alpha^2\sigma^2}{4},
 \qquad
 \mu_R=\frac{\alpha^2\sigma^2-4\omega}{8}.
\]
Equations~\eqref{eq:affine-sqrt-drift} and
\eqref{eq:affine-sqrt-variance} give
\[
 \mathbb{E}\xi(x)=-\frac{\mu_R}{x}+O(x^{-2}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb{E}\xi(x)^2=b+O(x^{-1}).
\]
In general,
\[
 \frac{2\mu_R}{b}=2\kappa+1>1.
\]

We verify Theorem~8.2 and Corollary~8.3 of
\citet{denisov2025markov}.  Set \(s(x)=x^{1/2}\), and use the truncated
moments \(\mu_j^{[s]}(x)\) defined above.
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-uniform-root-increments} implies, by choosing an
arbitrarily high moment order, that truncation changes either of the
preceding moment expansions by less than any prescribed inverse power of
\(x\).  Hence
\[
 \frac{2\mu_1^{[s]}(x)}{\mu_2^{[s]}(x)}
 =-\frac{2\kappa+1}{x}+O(x^{-2}).
\]
Choose \(0<\eta<\min(1,2\kappa)\), let
\(p(x)=x^{-1-\eta}\) for all sufficiently
large \(x\), and choose a positive decreasing continuously differentiable
function \(r\) that equals \((2\kappa+1)/x\) there.  Then
\[
 \frac{2\mu_1^{[s]}(x)}{\mu_2^{[s]}(x)}
 =-r(x)+o(p(x)),
 \qquad r'(x)=O(x^{-2}),\quad p'(x)=O(x^{-2}).
\]
For the functions used in the cited result, define, for \(x\geq0\),
\[
 \mathcal R(x)=\int_0^x r(z)\,dz,
 \qquad
 \mathcal U(x)=\int_0^x e^{\mathcal R(z)}\,dz,
\]
and set \(\mathcal U(x)=0\) for \(x<0\), as in the cited theorem.
There are positive constants \(C_{\mathcal R},C_{\mathcal U}\) such that
\(e^{\mathcal R(x)}\sim C_{\mathcal R}x^{2\kappa+1}\) and
\(\mathcal U(x)\sim C_{\mathcal U}x^{2\kappa+2}\).

The same uniform increment-moment bound verifies all four jump-tail
conditions of that result.  More explicitly,
\[
 \sup_{x\geq0}\frac{\mathbb{E}\mathcal U(\xi(x))}
                         {1+\mathcal U(x)}<\infty,
 \qquad
 \Pr\{|\xi(x)|>s(x)\}=o(p(x)/x),
\]
while
\[
 \mathbb{E}[|\xi(x)|^3\mathbf1_{\{|\xi(x)|\leq s(x)\}}]=O(1)
       =o(x^2p(x)),
 \qquad
 \mathbb{E}[\mathcal U(\xi(x))\mathbf1_{\{\xi(x)>s(x)\}}]
       =o(p(x)e^{\mathcal R(x)}).
\]
For the last relation, use the polynomial growth of \(\mathcal U\), the
uniform increment moments of every order, and
\(p(x)e^{\mathcal R(x)}\asymp x^{2\kappa-\eta}\to\infty\).


It remains to verify recurrence and nonconfinement.
Equation~\eqref{eq:affine-delta-mean} gives
\(\mathbb{E}[M_{t+1}-M_t\mid M_t=m]\leq\omega/2<0\) for all sufficiently large \(m\).
Applied to the stopped nonnegative state process, this drift bound implies
almost-sure returns of \(M_t\), and hence \(R_t=\sqrt{M_t}\), to a bounded
interval from every initial state.
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-boundary-nonconfinement} gives
\(\Pr(\limsup_{t\to\infty}R_t=\infty\mid R_0=x)=1\) for every \(x\).
Thus all hypotheses of the cited stationary-tail theorem are satisfied.
Since \(2\mu_R>b\), it yields
\[
 \Pr(R_0>x)\sim C_R\frac{x^2}{\mathcal U(x)}
              \sim \widetilde C_Rx^{-2\kappa}
\]
for positive constants \(C_R,\widetilde C_R\).  Substituting
\(x=\sqrt y\) proves \eqref{eq:affine-boundary-state-tail}.  The tail
integral formula shows that \(\mathbb{E} M_0^s<\infty\) exactly when
\(s<\kappa\), including divergence at \(s=\kappa\).
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-state-observation-moments} transfers the same
classification to \(X_0\).

label: lem:kappa-two-three-persistence
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Persistence from a high state

title: Proof
body_md:
Equation~\eqref{eq:affine-delta-mean} and positivity of the softplus
remainder imply, for all sufficiently large \(x\),
\[
 \omega\leq\mathbb{E}(M_{t+1}-M_t\mid M_t=x)\leq\omega/2<0.
\]
Since \(s_c\) is one-Lipschitz and
\(\operatorname{Var}(X_t\mid M_t=x)=\sigma^2x\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(M_{t+1}\mid M_t=x)\leq\alpha^2\sigma^2x.
\]

Starting from \(M_0=m\), let
\[
 \tau_m=\inf\{k\geq0:M_k\notin[m/2,2m]\},
 \qquad k_m=\lfloor a_{\rm per}m\rfloor,
\]
and define the stopped martingale
\[
 \mathcal M_\ell=\sum_{k=0}^{\ell-1}
 [M_{k+1}-M_k-\mathbb{E}(M_{k+1}-M_k\mid M_k)]
 \mathbf1_{\{k<\tau_m\}}.
\]
For all large \(m\),
\[
 \mathbb{E}[\mathcal M_{k_m}^2\mid M_0=m]\leq2\alpha^2\sigma^2mk_m.
\]
Choose \(a_{\rm per}>0\) so small that
\[
 |\omega|a_{\rm per}<\frac18,\qquad
 32\alpha^2\sigma^2a_{\rm per}<\frac14.
\]
Enlarge \(m_0\), if necessary, so that every point of
\([m/2,2m]\) lies in the region where the preceding drift bounds hold.
Doob's inequality then gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\max_{\ell\leq k_m}|\mathcal M_\ell|\geq m/4\,\middle|\,M_0=m\right)\leq\frac14.
\]
On the complementary event, the accumulated drift is bounded below by
\(-|\omega|k_m\) and is nonpositive.  If a first exit occurred by
\(k_m\), the stopped decomposition evaluated at that exit would place
the state strictly inside \([m/2,2m]\), a contradiction.  Thus
\[
 \Pr(M_k\in[m/2,2m],\ 0\leq k\leq k_m\mid M_0=m)\geq\frac34.
\]

Chebyshev's inequality and
\(\operatorname{Var}(X_0\mid M_0=m)=\sigma^2m\) give
\[
 \Pr(X_0<m/2\mid M_0=m)\leq\frac{4\sigma^2}{m}.
\]
On the state-persistence event \(M_j\geq m/2\), conditioning on \(M_j\)
and applying Chebyshev's inequality again gives
\[
 \Pr(\text{state persistence},\ X_j<m/4\mid M_0=m)
 \leq\frac{8\sigma^2}{m}.
\]
A union bound proves
\eqref{eq:kappa-two-three-persistence}, after increasing \(m_0\) and
reducing the probability constant.

label: lem:qmle-contrast-envelope
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:qmle-contrast-envelope}
Let \(m_t(\theta)>0\) be a stationary
\(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable candidate filter and let \(M_t\) be the true
conditional mean.  For
\[
 L_t(\theta)
 =X_t\log\frac{m_t(\theta)}{M_t}
  -(m_t(\theta)-M_t),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 L_t(\theta)\leq
 \bar L_t:=X_t\log\frac{X_t}{M_t}-X_t+M_t
 \leq\frac{(X_t-M_t)^2}{M_t},
 \qquad \mathbb{E} \bar L_t\leq\sigma_0^2,
 \label{eq:qmle-contrast-upper-envelope}
\end{equation}
where \(0\log0=0\).  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}[L_t(\theta)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 =-M_t \mathfrak h\!\left(\frac{m_t(\theta)}{M_t}\right),
 \qquad \mathfrak h(r)=r-1-\log r.
 \label{eq:qmle-conditional-contrast}
\end{equation}
The integrable upper bound makes the unconditional expectation
\(\mathbb{E} L_t(\theta)\) well defined as an extended real number in
\([-\infty,0]\); it need not be finite.

title: Proof
body_md:

\(x\log(\mu/m)-(\mu-m)\) over \(\mu>0\) gives its value at \(\mu=x\), with the
usual boundary interpretation at \(x=0\).  Also
\(y\log y-y+1\leq(y-1)^2\) for \(y\geq0\).  These two observations give
the inequalities in \eqref{eq:qmle-contrast-upper-envelope}; conditional
expectation and
\(\mathbb{E}[(X_t-M_t)^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=\sigma_0^2M_t\) give its final
claim.  Taking conditional expectation of the contrast gives
\eqref{eq:qmle-conditional-contrast}.

label: lem:affine-qmle-envelopes
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:affine-qmle-envelopes}
Let the parameters range over the compact set \(\Theta_Q\) in
Theorem~\ref{thm:affine-qmle}, and let \(\rho_\beta\in(0,1)\) bound the absolute
coefficient on the lagged filter.  If \(X_0\in L^2\), the stationary
candidate filters in Lemma~\ref{lem:unrestricted-candidate-filter}, their first
derivatives, the quasi-likelihood, the score, and the sample-information
integrand have the integrable uniform envelopes used below.  If
\(X_0\in L^3\), the same is true for the second derivatives and the full
Hessian envelope.  These conclusions hold for every affine conditional
family in Assumption~\ref{ass:affine-seed}.
head: environment
name: QMLE envelopes

title: Proof
body_md:
The calculus bounds used throughout this proof are collected in
Lemma~\ref{lem:softplus-calculus}.

Lemma~\ref{lem:unrestricted-candidate-filter} proves existence, uniqueness, and
initialization stability of every candidate filter, including candidates
with \(\alpha+\beta\geq1\).  Choose
\(\bar\rho\in(\sqrt{\rho_\beta},1)\).  {Define
\[
 Z_t:=\sum_{j\geq0}\bar\rho^j(1+X_{t-1-j}).
\]
Then the level envelope satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sup_\theta M_t(\theta)\leq CZ_t.
 \label{eq:qmle-level-envelope}
\end{equation}
}
For filters with two starting values, one of which may be the stationary
random initialization, the lemma gives
\begin{equation}
 \sup_\theta|M_t(\theta)-\widetilde M_t(\theta)|
 \leq\rho_\beta^t\sup_\theta|M_0(\theta)-\widetilde M_0(\theta)|.
 \label{eq:qmle-filter-initialization}
\end{equation}

Differentiating the candidate recursion gives
\[
 D_t(\theta)=s_c'(\eta_t(\theta))
 [e_t(\theta)+\beta D_{t-1}(\theta)]
\]
and
\[
 J_t(\theta)=\beta D_{t-1}^{(2)}(\theta)
  +e_\beta D_{t-1}(\theta)^\top+D_{t-1}(\theta)e_\beta^\top,
\]
\[
 D_t^{(2)}(\theta)=s_c''(\eta_t(\theta))
 A_t(\theta)A_t(\theta)^\top
 +s_c'(\eta_t(\theta))J_t(\theta),
 \qquad A_t(\theta)=e_t(\theta)+\beta D_{t-1}(\theta).
\]
Since \(0<s_c'\leq1\), \(0\leq s_c''\leq1/(4c)\), and
\(|\beta|\leq\rho_\beta\), iteration yields
\[
 \sup_\theta\|D_t(\theta)\|\leq C Z_t,\qquad
 \sup_\theta[\|J_t(\theta)\|+\|D_t^{(2)}(\theta)\|]\leq C Z_t^2.
\]
Here \(\bar\rho^2>\rho_\beta\) makes the iteration of the quadratic forcing term
geometrically summable.
Minkowski's and H\"older's inequalities show that \(Z_t\) has every
moment available for \(X_t\), in particular the orders needed below.

Compactness and
\eqref{eq:qmle-level-envelope} also give
\(\sup_\theta|\eta_t(\theta)|\leq C Z_t\).  Using
\eqref{eq:softplus-self-regularization} in the score and in
\(\mathcal H_t(\theta)\), the preceding bounds yield
\begin{align}
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_Q}|\ell_t^Q(\theta)|
 &\leq C(1+X_t)(1+Z_t),\label{eq:qmle-full-likelihood-envelope}\\
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_Q}\|\partial_\theta\ell_t^Q(\theta)\|
 &\leq C(1+X_t)(1+Z_t),\label{eq:qmle-full-score-envelope}\\
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_Q}
 \|\partial_{\theta\theta^\top}^2\ell_t^Q(\theta)\|
 &\leq C(1+X_t)(1+Z_t^2).
 \label{eq:qmle-full-hessian-envelope}
\end{align}
For example, before taking suprema over \(\theta\), the two Hessian terms are
bounded by constant multiples of \(X_t\|A_t(\theta)\|^2\) and
\((1+X_t)[\|A_t(\theta)\|^2+\|J_t(\theta)\|]\), respectively.  If
\(X_0\in L^3\), H\"older's inequality makes the last display
integrable; the first two displays require only second moments.  Notice
that this argument concerns moments under the true stationary law, not
stationarity of the candidate parameter.

label: lem:qmle-initialization
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:qmle-initialization}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:affine-qmle}, let stationary and
initialized candidate filters be driven by the same observations.  On
every compact subset \(\mathcal K\subseteq\Theta_Q\),
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^\infty\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}
 \left[
 |\widetilde\ell_t^Q(\theta)-\ell_t^Q(\theta)|
 +\|\widetilde S_t(\theta)-S_t(\theta)\|
 +\|\widetilde K_t(\theta)-K_t(\theta)\|
 \right]<\infty
 \quad\text{a.s.}
\]
These conclusions require only
\(\mathbb{E} X_0<\infty\).
head: environment
name: Initialization of the criterion, score, and information

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof follows the perturbed-recursion strategy of
\citet[Section~2]{straumannMikosch2006}, retaining explicit bounds to obtain
all three summability conclusions.
In this proof, filter quantities are evaluated at a generic
\(\theta\in\mathcal K\), whose argument is suppressed.
Untilded quantities use the stationary candidate filter, and tildes denote
its fixed-initialization counterpart.  Since \(\widetilde M_0>0\) is
independent of \(\theta\), \(\widetilde D_0=0\); subsequent derivatives
are obtained by differentiating the same forward recursion.
Let
\[
 B_0=1+\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}\left[
 |\widetilde M_0(\theta)-M_0(\theta)|
 +\|\widetilde D_0(\theta)-D_0(\theta)\|\right].
\]
The stationary envelopes and fixed initialization give \(B_0<\infty\) almost
surely.
Lemma~\ref{lem:unrestricted-candidate-filter} gives
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}|\widetilde M_t-M_t|\leq B_0\rho_\beta^t,
 \qquad
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}|\widetilde\eta_t-\eta_t|
 \leq B_0\rho_\beta^t.
\]
The \(1/c\)-Lipschitz property of \(\log s_c\) and the one-Lipschitz
property of \(s_c\) give
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}|\widetilde\ell_t^Q-\ell_t^Q|
 \leq CB_0\rho_\beta^t(1+X_t).
\]

Use the level envelope \(Z_t\) from \eqref{eq:qmle-level-envelope}, with
\(\bar\rho\in(\sqrt{\rho_\beta},1)\).  Since
\(\mathbb{E} Z_0=(1+\mathbb{E} X_0)/(1-\bar\rho)<\infty\), this envelope requires only
the assumed first moment.
Subtracting their recursions, using boundedness of \(s_c''\), and iterating
gives
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}
 [\|\widetilde A_t-A_t\|+\|\widetilde D_t-D_t\|]
 \leq CB_0\rho_\beta^t\sum_{j=1}^t(1+Z_j).
 \label{eq:qmle-initialized-first-derivative}
\end{equation}
Use \(p_c,r_c,j_c\) as defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:softplus-calculus}.  Since
\[
 S_t(\theta)=(X_t r_c(\eta_t)-p_c(\eta_t))A_t,
 \qquad
 K_t(\theta)=j_c(\eta_t)A_tA_t^\top,
\]
the preceding bounds and \(\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}\|A_t(\theta)\|\leq CZ_t\)
give
\begin{align}
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}\|\widetilde S_t-S_t\|
 &\leq CB_0\rho_\beta^t(1+X_t)
       \left[1+Z_t+\sum_{j=1}^t(1+Z_j)\right],
 \label{eq:qmle-score-initialization-bound}\\
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal K}\|\widetilde K_t-K_t\|
 &\leq C\left[
 B_0\rho_\beta^t(1+Z_t)
 \left(1+Z_t+\sum_{j=1}^t(1+Z_j)\right)
 +B_0^2\rho_\beta^{2t}
   \left(\sum_{j=1}^t(1+Z_j)\right)^2
 \right].
 \label{eq:qmle-information-initialization-bound}
\end{align}
If a stationary nonnegative process \((Y_t)\) satisfies
\(\mathbb{E}\log(1+Y_0)<\infty\), then \(b_{\mathrm{BC}}^{-t}Y_t\to0\) almost surely for every
\(b_{\mathrm{BC}}>1\): the tail-sum formula gives
\(\sum_t\Pr\{\log(1+Y_t)>t\log b_{\mathrm{BC}}\}<\infty\), so Borel--Cantelli applies.
Since \(X_t\) and the level envelope \(Z_t\) are integrable, this applies to
both.  Increase \(\rho_\beta\) slightly, without changing notation, and choose
\(b_{\mathrm{BC}}>1\) with \(\rho_\beta b_{\mathrm{BC}}^2<1\).  Almost surely, eventually,
\[
 1+X_t\leq Cb_{\mathrm{BC}}^t,\qquad 1+Z_t\leq Cb_{\mathrm{BC}}^t,
 \qquad \sum_{j=1}^t(1+Z_j)\leq Cb_{\mathrm{BC}}^t,
\]
with finite random \(C\).  Substitution into the criterion bound and
\eqref{eq:qmle-score-initialization-bound}--
\eqref{eq:qmle-information-initialization-bound} gives summable geometric
majorants because \(\rho_\beta b_{\mathrm{BC}}^2<1\); the factors \(B_0,B_0^2\) are almost
surely finite.  This proves all three assertions under a first moment.

label: lem:qmle-rare-relative-innovation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:qmle-rare-relative-innovation}
Let \((M_t,X_t)\) be the stationary solution under
Assumptions~\ref{ass:affine-seed} and \ref{ass:invertibility}, with
\(\phi_0=1\), \(\omega_0<0\), and \(\mathbb{E} M_t<\infty\).
For the innovations \(U_t=X_t-M_t\), define
\[
 \mathsf V_t(r)=1+\sum_{j=0}^\infty r^j|U_{t-1-j}|,\qquad 0<r<1.
\]
Fix \(\varrho\in(0,1)\), and write \(\mathsf V_t=\mathsf V_t(\varrho)\).
Then \(\mathsf V_t\in L^2\).  For every \(\chi\geq1\), there is
\(C_{0,\chi}<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}\left[\mathsf V_t^{\chi}
 \mathbf1_{\{\mathsf V_t>C_{0,\chi}(1+M_t)\}}\right]<\infty.
 \label{eq:qmle-rare-relative-moment}
\end{equation}
The assertion remains valid after increasing \(C_{0,\chi}\).
head: environment
name: Rare relative innovations at the stationary unit root

title: Proof
body_md:
At the unit root, \(\alpha_0=1-\beta_0>0\) and
\(M_{t+1}=s_c(\omega_0+M_t+\alpha_0U_t)\).
The affine conditional variance gives
\(\mathbb{E} U_t^2=\sigma_0^2\mathbb{E} M_t<\infty\), so Minkowski's inequality gives
\(\mathsf V_t\in L^2\).

Choose \(\varrho_0\in(\varrho,1)\) and then \(\epsilon>0\) so that
\(1-\alpha_0\epsilon>\varrho_0\).  Set
\[
 B_t=\mathbf1_{\{|U_t|>\epsilon(1+M_t)\}}.
\]
Since \(s_c(x)\geq x\), on \(\{B_t=0\}\),
\[
 1+M_{t+1}\geq(1-\alpha_0\epsilon)(1+M_t)+\omega_0
             \geq \varrho_0(1+M_t)+\omega_0.
\]
After enlarging fixed constants, the following inequality is therefore
valid on both \(\{B_t=0\}\) and \(\{B_t=1\}\):
\begin{equation}
 1+M_t\leq \varrho_0^{-1}(1+M_{t+1})+K
 +C(1+M_t+|U_t|)B_t.
 \label{eq:qmle-backward-good-bad}
\end{equation}
Define
\[
 \Sigma_t=\sum_{j\geq0}\varrho^j(1+M_{t-1-j}),
 \qquad
 \Xi_t=\sum_{j\geq0}\varrho^j
 (1+M_{t-1-j}+|U_{t-1-j}|)B_{t-1-j}.
\]
Multiplying \eqref{eq:qmle-backward-good-bad} at time \(t-1-j\) by
\(\varrho^j\) and summing gives
\[
 \Sigma_t\leq \varrho_0^{-1}(1+M_t+\varrho\Sigma_t)
 +\frac K{1-\varrho}+C\Xi_t,
\]
and hence \(\Sigma_t\leq C_\Sigma(1+M_t+\Xi_t)\) for some finite
positive deterministic constant \(C_\Sigma\), depending only on the fixed
model parameters and the choices of \(\varrho,\varrho_0,\epsilon\).
Set \(C_{\rm rel}=1+\epsilon C_\Sigma\).  Splitting the innovations according
to \(B_{t-1-j}\) yields
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf V_t\leq1+\epsilon\Sigma_t+\Xi_t
 \leq C_{\rm rel}(1+M_t+\Xi_t).
 \label{eq:qmle-V-good-bad}
\end{equation}
If \(C_0>2C_{\rm rel}\), then on
\(\{\mathsf V_t>C_0(1+M_t)\}\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf V_t\leq2C_{\rm rel}\Xi_t.
 \label{eq:qmle-V-by-Xi}
\end{equation}

Weighted Jensen's inequality gives, for every \(\chi\geq1\),
\begin{equation}
 \Xi_t^{\chi}\leq C_{\chi,\varrho}\sum_{j\geq0}
 \varrho^{j(\chi+1)/2}
 (1+M_{t-1-j}+|U_{t-1-j}|)^{\chi}B_{t-1-j}.
 \label{eq:qmle-weighted-bad-sum}
\end{equation}
Since \(\mathcal L(U_t\mid M_t=m)=\mathcal L(U_m)\),
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration} gives, for arbitrary \(p\geq2\),
\[
 \mathbb{E}(|U_t|^p\mid M_t=m)\leq C_p(1+m^{p/2}).
\]
Choose \(p>\chi\) and \(p\geq2(\chi-1)\).  Markov's inequality gives, uniformly
for \(m\geq1\),
\[
 (1+m)^{\chi}\Pr(B_t=1\mid M_t=m)
 +\mathbb{E}(|U_t|^{\chi}B_t\mid M_t=m)
 \leq C_{\chi}(1+m).
\]
The uniform small-state conditional moments in
Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-concentration} give the same bound for \(0<m<1\).
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}[(1+M_t+|U_t|)^{\chi}B_t\mid M_t=m]
 \leq C_{\chi}(1+m).
 \label{eq:qmle-one-bad-moment}
\end{equation}
Taking expectations in \eqref{eq:qmle-weighted-bad-sum} and using
stationarity and \(\mathbb{E} M_t<\infty\) gives \(\mathbb{E}\Xi_t^{\chi}<\infty\).
Equation~\eqref{eq:qmle-V-by-Xi} proves
\eqref{eq:qmle-rare-relative-moment}.

label: lem:boundary-qmle-hessian-envelope
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Boundary likelihood envelopes under a first moment

label: eq:qmle-backward-level-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
Use the true state \(M_t\) and the innovations \(U_t\) defined above.
Choose \(\bar\rho\in(\sqrt{\rho_\beta},1)\), where
\(\sup_{\Theta_Q}|\beta|\leq\rho_\beta<1\), and specialize the
innovation envelope to \(\mathsf V_t=\mathsf V_t(\bar\rho)\).
The preceding lemma gives \(\mathsf V_t\in L^2\) and its rare-event moments of
every order.  Since \(s_c(x)\geq x\), the true boundary recursion gives
\[
 M_{t-1}\leq M_t+|\omega_0|+\alpha_0|U_{t-1}|.
\]
Iteration yields, for every \(k\geq1\),
\begin{equation}
 M_{t-k}\leq M_t+k|\omega_0|
       +\alpha_0\sum_{\ell=1}^k|U_{t-\ell}|.
 \label{eq:qmle-backward-level-bound}
\end{equation}
Moreover, \(X_{t-k}\leq M_{t-k}+|U_{t-k}|\).  Recalling the level envelope
\(Z_t\) in \eqref{eq:qmle-level-envelope}, substitute
\eqref{eq:qmle-backward-level-bound} with \(k=j+1\) and interchange the two
nonnegative sums.  Because
\[
 \sum_{j\geq0}\bar\rho^j
       \sum_{\ell=1}^{j+1}|U_{t-\ell}|
 =\frac1{1-\bar\rho}
   \sum_{\ell\geq1}\bar\rho^{\ell-1}|U_{t-\ell}|,
\]
and \(\sum_{j\geq0}(j+1)\bar\rho^j<\infty\), this gives
\begin{equation}
 Z_t\leq C(M_t+\mathsf V_t).
 \label{eq:qmle-boundary-current-state-envelope}
\end{equation}

Using \(X_{t-1}=M_{t-1}+U_{t-1}\) and \(\phi_0=1\), we have
\[
 \eta_t(\theta)-\eta_t(\theta_0)
 = (\omega-\omega_0)+(\alpha-\alpha_0)U_{t-1}
   +(\phi-1)M_{t-1}+\beta \delta_{t-1}(\theta).
\]
For sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), define the closed ball
\[
 \mathcal N_\varepsilon
 =\{\theta\in\mathbb R^3:\|\theta-\theta_0\|\leq\varepsilon\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{int}(\Theta_Q).
\]
The one-Lipschitz property of softplus and the uniform bound on \(|\beta|\)
then give
\begin{align}
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}|\delta_t(\theta)|
 &\leq C\varepsilon(M_t+\mathsf V_t),
 \label{eq:qmle-local-filter-boundary}\\
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}\|A_t(\theta)\|
 &\leq C(M_t+\mathsf V_t),\qquad
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}\|J_t(\theta)\|
 \leq C(M_t+\mathsf V_t)^2.
 \label{eq:qmle-local-derivatives-boundary}
\end{align}
Indeed, the preceding identity gives the one-step bound
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}|\delta_t(\theta)|
 \leq C\varepsilon(1+M_{t-1}+|U_{t-1}|)
 +\rho_\beta\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}|\delta_{t-1}(\theta)|.
\]
Iteration and \eqref{eq:qmle-backward-level-bound} prove
\eqref{eq:qmle-local-filter-boundary}.  Iterating the derivative recursions
in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-qmle-envelopes}, using
\eqref{eq:qmle-boundary-current-state-envelope}, proves
\eqref{eq:qmle-local-derivatives-boundary}; here
\(\bar\rho^2>\rho_\beta\) controls the quadratic forcing.

We next prove that
\(\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}\|J_t(\theta)\|\) is integrable.
The chain rule gives
\(D_t(\theta)=s_c'(\eta_t(\theta))A_t(\theta)\).  Define
\[
 D_t^*=\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}\|D_t(\theta)\|,
 \qquad
 J_t^*=\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}\|J_t(\theta)\|.
\]
Then \(\mathbb{E} D_t^*<\infty\).  Split the candidates according as
\(M_t(\theta)\geq M_t/2\).  On this set,
\eqref{eq:qmle-sharp-softplus-derivatives} and
\eqref{eq:qmle-local-derivatives-boundary} give the bound below; on its
complement, \eqref{eq:qmle-local-filter-boundary} gives
\(M_t+\mathsf V_t\leq C\mathsf V_t\), and boundedness of \(s_c''\) gives the same bound:
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon}
 s_c''(\eta_t(\theta))\|A_t(\theta)\|^2
 \leq C(1+\mathsf V_t^2).
\]
The recursion for \(J_t(\theta)\) becomes
\[
 J_t(\theta)=e_\beta D_{t-1}(\theta)^\top
 +D_{t-1}(\theta)e_\beta^\top
 +\beta\bigl[s_c''(\eta_{t-1}(\theta))
 A_{t-1}(\theta)A_{t-1}(\theta)^\top
 +s_c'(\eta_{t-1}(\theta))J_{t-1}(\theta)\bigr].
\]
Taking suprema gives \(J_t^*\leq\rho_\beta J_{t-1}^*+F_{t-1}\) for an integrable stationary
\(F_t\).  Backward iteration gives
\[
 J_t^*\leq\rho_\beta^kJ_{t-k}^*
 +\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\rho_\beta^jF_{t-1-j}.
\]
Stationarity makes the first term converge to zero in probability, hence
almost surely along a deterministic subsequence.  Passing to that
subsequence gives
\(J_t^*\leq\sum_{j\geq0}\rho_\beta^jF_{t-1-j}\) almost surely.  The right side
has expectation \((1-\rho_\beta)^{-1}\mathbb{E} F_0\), and therefore
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E} J_t^*<\infty.
 \label{eq:qmle-integrable-J}
\end{equation}

It remains to transfer these predictor bounds to the likelihood Hessian and
information integrand.  Use \(p_c,r_c,r_c'\) from
Lemma~\ref{lem:softplus-calculus}.  Suppressing the generic candidate
argument \(\theta\) in \(\mathcal H_t,K_t,\eta_t,A_t,J_t\), direct
differentiation gives
\[
 \mathcal H_t=-X_t r_c'(\eta_t)A_tA_t^\top
     +s_c''(\eta_t)A_tA_t^\top
     +(p_c(\eta_t)-X_t r_c(\eta_t))J_t,
 \qquad K_t=\frac{p_c(\eta_t)^2}{M_t(\theta)}A_tA_t^\top.
\]
Split \(\mathcal N_\varepsilon\) into
\[
 \mathcal C_t=\{\theta\in \mathcal N_\varepsilon:M_t(\theta)\geq M_t/2\},
 \qquad \mathcal D_t=\mathcal N_\varepsilon\setminus\mathcal C_t.
\]
For \(\mathcal A_t\in\{\mathcal C_t,\mathcal D_t\}\), let
\(\mathcal H_{t,\mathcal A}^*=\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal A_t}
\|\mathcal H_t(\theta)\|\) and define \(K_{t,\mathcal A}^*\) analogously,
with an empty supremum equal to zero.  Continuity makes these restricted
suprema measurable (use a measurable maximum argument on \(\mathcal C_t\)
and a fixed countable dense subset on the relatively open \(\mathcal D_t\)).
On \(\mathcal C_t\),
Lemma~\ref{lem:softplus-calculus},
\eqref{eq:qmle-local-derivatives-boundary}, and
\(\mathbb{E}(1+X_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=1+M_t\) give
\[
 \mathbb{E}(\mathcal H_{t,\mathcal C}^*\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})
 +K_{t,\mathcal C}^*
 \leq C\left[\frac{(M_t+\mathsf V_t)^2}{1+M_t}+J_t^*\right].
\]
If \(\mathcal D_t\ne\varnothing\),
\eqref{eq:qmle-local-filter-boundary} gives
\(M_t\leq C\varepsilon\mathsf V_t\) and
\(M_t+\mathsf V_t\leq C\mathsf V_t\).  The globally bounded quantities
\(r_c,r_c',s_c'',p_c\), and \(p_c^2/s_c\) therefore give
\[
 \mathbb{E}(\mathcal H_{t,\mathcal D}^*\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})
 +K_{t,\mathcal D}^*
 \leq C(1+M_t)\mathsf V_t^2
       \mathbf1_{\{\mathcal D_t\ne\varnothing\}}.
\]
Choose \(C_0\) from
\eqref{eq:qmle-rare-relative-moment} at power three and then decrease
\(\varepsilon\), if necessary, so that, on \(\{M_t>1\}\),
\(\{\mathcal D_t\ne\varnothing\}\subseteq
\{\mathsf V_t>C_0(1+M_t)\}\).  Hence the last display is bounded by
\[
 C\left[\mathsf V_t^2+
 \mathsf V_t^3\mathbf1_{\{\mathsf V_t>C_0(1+M_t)\}}\right].
\]
Finally,
\((M_t+\mathsf V_t)^2/(1+M_t)
 \leq C(1+M_t+\mathsf V_t^2)\).  Taking expectations and using
\(\mathbb{E} M_t<\infty\), \(\mathsf V_t\in L^2\),
\eqref{eq:qmle-integrable-J}, and
\eqref{eq:qmle-rare-relative-moment} proves both envelopes in
\eqref{eq:qmle-boundary-local-envelopes} with
\(\mathcal N=\mathcal N_\varepsilon\) for this fixed \(\varepsilon\).
